description: Traffic Signal Re-Timing is a dataset listed in City of Austin open data portal (datahub.austintexas.gov), an open data portal (Socrata) of a city, published or maintained by City of Austin. This dataset reports the progress of the Austin Transportation and Public Works Annual Signal Timing Program. Traffic signal engineers re-time approximately 1/3 of the city’s 1,000+ signals each year, with the goal of ensuring signals are timed for optimum safety and performance. Coverage: Austin. The portal files it under the category Transportation and Mobility. Its tags are transportation, transit, traffic signals, re-timing, mobility. The table has 11 columns. Attribution on the portal: City of Austin, Texas - data.austintexas.gov. The portal shows 2023-07-20 as the last data update. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is public domain (as labelled on the portal). Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support traffic, parking and road network studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-soc-datahub-austintexas-gov-portal.
